notes.fact: Zelensky says Russia fired 289 drones, 17 ballistic and 59 cruise missiles overnight; DTEK says three of its five thermal plants went offline.

notes.fact: Kremlin spokesman Peskov confirmed a Russian delegation led by aide Vladimir Medinsky will attend US-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11.
Zelensky said he spoke with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner before the talks and asked for Patriot air-defence systems to protect lives.
Russia's defence ministry says drones hit a Nova Poshta terminal near Kharkiv and a 330-kV substation in Dnipropetrovsk; Ukraine hit Ryazan, with injuries reported on both sides.
Newsweek reports a Russian strike on a Kharkiv hospital injured 73 people, per Zelensky, and that Ukraine's prime minister named plants hit in Kharkiv, Dnipropetrovsk and Vinnytsia regions.

notes.fact: Russia's defence ministry said on Nov 2 it hit a cargo vessel used for military purposes 58 km south of Odesa; an Odesa official separately reported four people injured in an attack.
notes.event: Russian strike on cargo ship off Odesa

notes.fact: The tanker Mentor, damaged in a Russian drone attack off Odesa on Sept 24, broke from its tow in a storm; Romania rescued three tug crew and Bulgaria is tracking it.
notes.event: Drifting tanker Mentor near Romania and Bulgaria

notes.fact: Trump told Fox News the US must do something large against Iran, saying any action could be a heavy hit, per BBC as relayed by Gulf News.

notes.event: Trump signals possible major strike on Iran

notes.fact: Reuters, via The New Arab, reports Houthis took Al-Maqatirah district and were fighting at a camp at Tur al-Bahah, about 80 km from Aden, citing sources.
Government-aligned field sources say forces backed by the Giants Brigades retook positions in Al-Maqatirah on Nov 4 and blocked Houthi pushes toward Tur al-Baha.
Government-aligned TV channels report airstrikes on Houthi launchers in Ibb and Lahj, and eight civilians killed or hurt by a Houthi missile in Taiz's Hayfan district.

A government military official told Xinhua two Houthi ballistic missiles hit a Lahj market on Nov 3, killing one and wounding 10; Houthi spokesman Sarea denied any operation toward Saudi territory that day.
Houthi-run al-Masirah TV says an airstrike it blames on Saudi warplanes hit a footwear factory north of Taiz on Nov 3, killing three and wounding eight.
Türkiye Today says the Houthis announced on Nov 4 they fired a ballistic missile at Riyadh's King Khalid airport; independent confirmation of impact was not given.
Stars and Stripes says a Somali outlet reported US troops left Baledogle airfield; AFRICOM did not confirm, saying only that it repositions forces.
AFRICOM's press page lists a strike on al-Shabaab on Oct 23, later than the Oct 21 date in the tracker, so strikes have not paused for 30 days.
The UN Security Council Report's November forecast says al-Shabaab is using Somalia's political crisis to expand its territory and keeps launching deadly attacks in central and southern Somalia.
Sudan Tribune reports military sources said about 10 drones hit El Obeid on Oct 9, wounding six civilians; they blamed the RSF, which did not comment. No newer report found.
AFP reports drone strikes on a university dormitory and a displacement shelter in El Obeid killed at least 10 people; a local official blamed the RSF, which did not respond.
Dawn reports Pakistani and Afghan forces traded fire along the border on Nov 1, shutting Torkham for about five hours and killing one civilian by mortar near Angoor Adda.
Dawn says Torkham reopened after border officials agreed through intermediaries to halt construction near the border; tension stayed high at Angoor Adda, where Pakistan says it hit Afghan posts.

Iran's Kayhan relays Taliban-linked media: this was the third Torkham clash in a week; Pakistani shelling in Paktika's Shkin killed one civilian; UNAMA counts over 1,700 casualties from Oct 2025 to Sept 2026.
Tempo says a firefight on Oct 28 reportedly left two Afghan teenagers dead and a UN staff member hurt, and OCHA warned that Torkham fighting endangers civilians and aid workers.
DVB reports the Arakan Army says Nov 1 air strikes in four Rakhine townships killed at least 12 civilians and injured 32, including at a maternity clinic in Mrauk-U.
Reuters, via Straits Times, counted 15 dead including a newborn across Rakhine and Kayah; it says the Arakan Army, holding most of Rakhine, has neared Sittwe.
UNICEF said an air strike on a school for displaced children in Loikaw, Kayah state, killed at least three children; it did not name who carried it out.
Critical Threats says clashes continued in Walungu highlands and the Ruzizi foothills near Uvira with little change on the ground; the US sanctioned Rwanda's defence ministry.
notes.event: South Kivu fighting and US sanctions

notes.fact: SOS Médias Burundi reports rebel drone attacks led government-coalition fighters, including Burundian troops, to leave positions in the Bijombo highlands of Uvira territory; casualty figures were not confirmed.
A Kujenga Amani analysis says JNIM attacks disrupted fuel supply: tankers from Senegal halt at Kayes, and Bamako now gets fuel mainly via the Abidjan route and army-escorted convoys.
Haitian police found the burned truck used by the four missing Salvadoran technicians in Croix-des-Bouquets on Nov 3, but not the men; Bukele posted videos of troops patrolling.
Latin Times says Salvadoran armoured units launched a ground operation on Nov 2 against 400 Mawozo and Chen Mechan, reportedly killing at least a dozen fighters; the claim is unverified.
AP reports 400 Mawozo leader Wilson Joseph wrote UN chief Guterres on Nov 2 asking for a delegation for dialogue; the UN confirmed receipt, per a source.
Latin Times, citing Infobae, says Salvadoran troops set up a base in Tabarre near the US embassy; UN's Dujarric said most are outside the UN-backed force's mandate.
UN News reports Ethiopia told the Security Council Eritrean troops advanced up to 60 km into Tigray; Eritrea rejects this, and Guterres urged all parties to stop fighting. No newer report found.

Al Jazeera notes an analyst says Ethiopia's claims about Eritrean involvement are hard to verify independently; the TPLF-led alliance took Mekelle, withdrew Oct 3, and government-allied forces entered.
Responsible Statecraft, citing reports, says Ethiopian drones struck Eritrean forces near Adigrat, and an unnamed source told AFP 5,000-8,000 Eritrean troops are in Tigray.
notes.event: Drone strikes on Eritrean forces near Adigrat
